Add support for stereo recording

When enabled, the uplink is recorded to the left channel and the
downlink is recorded to the right channel. Due to AudioRecord's lack of
ability to get the hardware timestamps corresponding to an audio buffer
read, BCR just assumes that the uplink and downlink are synchronized and
that neither are dropping frames. Both channels are simply recorded
continuously.

This feature is currently only known to work in newer Google Pixel
devices that support simultaneous call recording and AI-related features
in the builtin dialer.

This commit also includes a few improvements:

* The recording loop now always attempts to wait until approximately
  half of the audio buffer is filled before looping again. Previously,
  the loop was only delayed when AudioRecord returned no data.

* The encoding loop now has a less aggressive 10ms timeout instead of
  500us when waiting for an input buffer to reduce busy waiting.

* There were a few areas where the frame rate was assumed to be the
  sample rate * the channel count, which is incorrect. The frame rate is
  always equal to the sample rate. This did not result in any bugs
  before because there was always just a single channel.

Use libphonenumber for phone number formatting

This fixes a few issues where Android's builtin PhoneNumberUtils fails
to format phone numbers with the requested formatting. For example, if
formatNumberToE164() is given a number without a country code, it
returns a string without a country code, which is not valid E.164.
libphonenumber is currently the state of the art for formatting phone
numbers properly.

With this commit, only libphonenumber's formatting methods are supported
now, which is partially a breaking change.

- {phone_number:E.164} is now guaranteed to be E.164-formatted
- {phone_number:international} has been added
- {phone_number:formatted} has been renamed to {phone_number:national}
  and will be automatically migrated
- {phone_number:national} will no longer implicitly fall back to
  {phone_number}
- {phone_number:digits_only} has been removed and will be automatically
  migrated to {phone_number}

Signed-off-by: Andrew Gunnerson <accounts+github@chiller3.com>

RecorderThread: Work around Android binder BR_FROZEN_REPLY error

For whatever reason, when calling DocumentsContract.createDocument()
for a URI served by local storage (com.android.externalstorage), the
binder call will fail with:

    W/libbinder.IPCThreadState(27223): Transaction failed because process frozen.
    I/binder  (27302): 27302:27223 dead process or thread
    E/libbinder.IPCThreadState(27223): Binder transaction failure. id: 3705901, cmd: BR_FROZEN_REPLY (29202), error: 0 (Success)
    D/ActivityThread(27223): Too many transaction errors, throttling freezer binder callback.
    E/JavaBinder(27223): !!! FAILED BINDER TRANSACTION !!!  (parcel size = 736)

This seems to happen more frequently when ending a call immediately
after connection or when receiving a call from a private number. There
is likely a horrible race condition somewhere in Android as these are
calls that any app is allowed to perform at any time. BCR isn't doing
anything out of the ordinary here.

After some experimentation, it looks like this can be worked around by
making binder calls to com.android.externalstorage sooner. This commit
adds a dumb query for the name of the output directory before the call
recording begins. This appears to be sufficient even after letting the
call stay active for several minutes and `dumpsys activity processes`
showing com.android.externalstorage as being frozen again.

Fixes: #638

Replace bottom sheets with regular preferences

This is a bit uglier visually than before, but the implementation is
much simpler. The goal is to fix layout issues with languages where
strings will inherently be long, like in German. Previously, it was
common to have text truncated and impossible to wrap due to quirks with
Android's ChipGroup implementation. Having plain old preferences also
lets us avoid numerous bottom sheet animation bugs in the material
components library.

This should also help folks who depend on accessibility services to use

Port to Jetpack Compose and adopt Material 3 Expressive

Google recently announced that they will be focusing their efforts on
Compose and all of the old View-based libraries are now in maintenance
mode [0][1].

This commit is a direct 1:1 port of the old UI to Compose. There are no
changes to the UX, but the UI now follows Material 3 Expressive design.
A couple of the old libraries are still kept around:

* material-components-android is still used for android:colorBackground
  in the View theme so that the splash screen and the area surrounding
  the Activity when using predictive back gestures has the same color as
  the app's background. The library's HCT color space utility classes
  are also still needed for the filename template syntax highlighter.

* preferences is still used just for the PreferenceManager class. The
  framework version of the class is deprecated.

The various screens in the app are still built around activities instead
of switching over to the new navigation3 library. This is an intentional
choice because navigation3 currently has no good mechanism for passing
around results in a locally scoped way (like Activity's setResult()) and
its predictive back animations don't look nearly as good as what Android
has builtin for activities.

Accessibility-wise, the experience should be equivalent to before. I've
tested using nearly all of the app's UI elements when navigating using
only the Talkback screen reader.

The main downside is that Compose makes the APK noticeably larger. Not
much can be done about that since we already enable all of R8's
optimizations.

[0] https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/first
[1] https://m3.material.io/blog/material-is-compose-first

Mark the final Ogg page as the end of the stream

AOSP's OggWriter copies its mReachedEOS field into every packet's e_o_s
field, but only sets that field to true after the write loop has already
exited. No page in the output file ever has the end-of-stream bit set in
its header type flags, so the logical bitstream is never terminated.

Demuxers that seek to the end of the file to find the last granule
position reject the result. Firefox is one, and refuses to play BCR's
recordings with NS_ERROR_DOM_MEDIA_METADATA_ERR.

Add an OggContainer that wraps MediaMuxer and, once the muxer has
finished writing, sets the end-of-stream bit in the last page's header
and recomputes that page's CRC. As with FlacContainer, this only runs
after the encoder signals EOF, so aborted recordings are untouched.

The page structure and CRC logic is split into OggPage, which has no
Android dependencies and is covered by JVM unit tests.
